title: Holographic brain paper and the rendering post: goals, claims, checks
how_to_read: goals: what we want to finish. A goal is met when every claim it needs holds and its done_when tests pass.
claims: what we think is true. Each names its kind and the check in 8_checks.py that tests it. A claim holds only if its check passes; agreement between reviewers counts for nothing.

kinds: quote (the paper's or her words, matched letter for letter), derived (exact algebra), number (arithmetic), rerun (floating-point simulation), cited (textbook physics), reading (a statement about what the paper contains, refuted by pointing at a line).
withdrawn: claims we made earlier and were wrong about, with what caught them.
files: every file the folder held at commit c3f17265a, and what became of it. Deleted files remain in git history at that commit.

claims.says: A record of which slit removes the stripes whether or not anyone reads it. Copying the record into a reader later leaves the screen pattern exactly as it was.
claims.rests_on: a finite two-path model; the same result is textbook quantum mechanics and is seen in many which-path experiments (cited)

claims.says: 'Does not render' read as 'rebuilt exactly whenever someone looks' gives every record the same chance as a world that was there all along, so under independent sampling the Bayes factor is 1 for any data.
Her post removes the computer from the analogy: 'The simulation isn't a giant computer'. A game's skipping needs a program, a computer, a screen and a player.
When a record is read never changes what was recorded: any operation on the record and its reader leaves the screen statistics unchanged.
claims.rests_on: the same finite model, with a random unitary on record and reader

claims.says: The paper never uses 'render'. Section 6 opens with the outside world as given. Section 5 calls how a quantum mind could perceive the macro-world 'yet another mystery altogether'.

Equal reports alone do not give a Bayes factor of 1 (9 in 10 against 5 in 10 gives 1.8); equal chances for every record, sampled independently, do. Without independence the product rule fails (factor 2).

A^0 = 0 with div A = 0 makes the left side of (A7) vanish, so the charge density is zero or constant in time; a constant density forces the two-level coherence R that drives (A38) to zero. Repair: A^0 from Poisson's equation, at the price of an electrostatic term.
From (A82)-(A86), d/dt(div E - J^0) = -M^2 div A - gamma div(E + grad A_0) + v div(A^(n-1) + A^(n+1)); the e^2 terms cancel. The boson number is conserved; Gauss's law is not.
At the paper's parameters the Gauss residual is 1.1 to 2.3 times the charge change the run produces, while the density dips match the paper's to within about 10 %.

The static inverse of (A82) carries d2^2 u1 where (A88) prints d1^2 u1; for targets (10)-(11) the corrected recursion u(n-1) = 2.5 u(n) - u(n+1) gives 2.13, not the 3.9 the text computes by dropping the backward term.
(A51) assumes the pattern |r + o|^2; in (A48) the external wave enters only through M^2; the screening number is 0.045 at the Section 4 values; (A52) contains the image |r|^2 o and the twin r^2 o*.

k_B T ln 2 = 18.5 meV at 310 K (the paper says 20), the 500 nm photon is 2.48 eV (2.4), the 60 um figure is hc/(k_B T ln 2); a one-year single-barrier record needs 1.20 eV for an attempt time of 1 ps, 0.46 eV for 1 s.

8.32e10 bit/mm^2 and 2.6 PB (the paper says 2.5) against 31.25 TB; a surface hologram holds 0.5 TB and the thickness factor n_r d / lambda = 5200 makes the difference; at 4 meV the wavelength is 310 um and the capacity 11 MB; at 1500 nm about 0.1 PB.

(A36)-(A38) conserve the energy (A39) and Z^2 + R^2; (A44)-(A45) solve (A43) with tau_R = 2 pi/(g^2 Omega N); at theta_0 = 0 there is no pulse; the Section 3 slab is 4000 wavelengths deep and about 1e6 across, against an emitter-size condition of one wavelength.

The density dip of Figure 6 is first order in the charge e: in (A86) the fluid moves with velocity (e/m) A, so the dip is the fluid carried by the longitudinal drive. A first-order estimate, 0.25 (1 - exp(-0.01 t)), gives 1.2, 4.5, 8.2, 15.8 and 21.6 % at t = 5, 20, 40, 100, 200 against the paper's 1.3, 4.5, 9.1, 16 and 21 %. In a rerun, halving e from 0.3 to 0.15 reduces the dip at t = 20 by 1.7, and halving again by 1.9 (an e^2 mechanism would give 4).
The paper attributes the slight distortions of Figure 6f to the Laplacian of |phi| in A_0, the only term carrying Planck's constant; a run without it has not been reported.
A 21 nm cutoff in a hollow guide passes only shorter wavelengths; as a dielectric rod of radius 12.5 nm (indices 1.5 and 1.33) the guide has V = 0.11 at 500 nm.

No equation in the paper takes a sense input, reads a stored pattern back, drives an action or stands for an experience; the only reader named is an external headset; the paper reports one simulation and no measurement of its own.

(A70) prints the wrong sign of the squared-velocity term (the free plane wave satisfies only the + form); (A76) and (A78) print e where (A82) has e^2, which leaves a remainder in the Gauss-law balance; the resonance threshold after (A47) is Omega^2 >= e^2 n/m.
1e-13 W at 500 nm is about 2.5e5 photons per second; writing 2.5 PB at one photon per bit from one such source takes about 2500 years.

Written as phi = R exp(i beta), (A63) is exactly the continuity equation (A69) and the balance (A70) with the + sign: a charged fluid. The Laplacian term in (A70), (A81) and (A87) is the only term that carries Planck's constant.

withdrawn.said: The density dip in Figure 6 is produced by the e^2 A^2/2m term and scales as e^2 (5_dissection.md before this rebuild, its statement 11).
withdrawn.why: In (A86) the density moves with velocity (e/m) A, so the dip is first order in e. A rerun at e = 0.3, 0.15 and 0.075 gives dips at t = 20 of 3.54, 2.07 and 1.08 %: halving e divides the dip by 1.7 and 1.9, not by 4 (P8). That the dip vanishes at e = 0 still stands.
withdrawn.caught_by: this rebuild, by trying to contradict the claim with reruns at three values of e

withdrawn.said: The dip deepens after the drive is gone.
withdrawn.why: The drive decays with gamma_2 = 0.01, so at t = 100 it is still at 37 %. The dip follows the time integral of the drive's divergence and stops growing only as the drive vanishes.

withdrawn.said: The resonance threshold is Omega >= e^2 n/m, copied from the paper.
withdrawn.why: The two sides have different units; the dispersion relation gives Omega^2 >= e^2 n/m.
withdrawn.caught_by: an outside review, checked by derivation (P12)

withdrawn.said: The lattice simulation fails to conserve the boson number.
withdrawn.why: It conserves it to 1e-6 %, as the paper says; what drifts is div E - J^0 (P2).
withdrawn.caught_by: an outside review, checked by rerun

withdrawn.said: Corner second differences of the target spoil the drive formula.
withdrawn.why: They enter only the misprinted (A88); the corrected inverse has no derivative terms for these targets (P3).
withdrawn.caught_by: an outside review, checked by derivation

withdrawn.said: A public reply quoted the vision sentence without the paper's 'perhaps'.
withdrawn.why: A misquote, however small, hands the reader a reason to doubt the rest. Every quote is now matched letter for letter by the checks.
